A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SHDD-based image geolocalization work, renamed from LocDiffusion to LocDiff. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original geolocalization experiments, gallery-generalization tests, computational measurements, and appendix ablations on encodings, perturbations, losses, and network width.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations on further datasets, comparisons with generative geolocalization methods, and additional computational measurements.

M1.justification: The SHDD encoding, KL-divergence objective, mode-seeking decoder, frozen CLIP conditioning, and CS-UNet remain unchanged. LocDiff-H retains the earlier LocDiffusion+GeoCLIP procedure of restricting retrieval to 200 km neighborhoods. New pseudocode and augmentation descriptions do not establish a new underlying method.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands beyond Im2GPS3k to YFCC-26k, GWS15k, OSV-5M, and YFCC-4k. This adds street-view coverage and, particularly, the GWS15k scenario whose spatial distribution differs from MP16. MP16 remains the stated training dataset for the GeoCLIP-style evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds evaluated comparisons with vMF, vMFMix, Diff R3, FM R3, and RFM S2, including a longer-trained RFM S2 variant. These introduce direct generative geolocalization comparators absent from v1. The original Im2GPS3k comparator set remains.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a separate generative-comparison setup and density/coverage metrics in Table 2. It also changes the reported DDPM sampling count from 100 to 200 and the main hybrid configuration from L=47 to L=23. These establish reported setting changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a reverse-diffusion trajectory visualization in Appendix A.1, a brief augmentation/averaging check reporting GeoCLIP street accuracy falling from about 14% to below 10%, and component timing analysis. Existing degree, gallery, encoder/decoder, perturbation, loss, and network-width ablation results are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run uncertainty. The 16 generated predictions are inference ensembles, not statistical replication of experiments.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add extensive benchmark and distribution-quality results. The Im2GPS3k hybrid row also changes: street accuracy becomes 15.3 instead of 14.4, for example, but its degree changes from L=47 to L=23, preventing a same-setting gain interpretation. The standalone L=47 Im2GPS3k scores and existing generalization/ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The principal SHDD definitions, KL/Wasserstein argument, decoder equations, and spherical-harmonic formulas are retained. v2 Section 5.3 adds a limited asymptotic complexity argument claiming O(1) encoding time under parallel evaluation and O(d) space; it does not add a new correctness proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion move from competitive geolocalization performance to state-of-the-art claims across five datasets, explicitly including superiority over coordinate-space generative methods. This substantially broadens the performance claim while retaining SHDD, CS-UNet, latent diffusion, and spatial generalizability as the central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains the hybrid's poorer GWS15k performance through harmful gallery bias under spatial distribution mismatch, adding an applicability qualification. Section 5.3 also proposes a multiscale explanation for faster convergence. The earlier resolution, quadratic-dimensionality, and numerical-stability limitations remain in Appendix A.4 despite being shortened in the conclusion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds training and inference pseudocode, and v2 explicitly identifies image augmentation within the existing 16-sample ensemble. It adds operation timings and revises the training-degree summary from 15/23/31 to 23/47. Most optimizer settings, hardware information, and detailed operations were already documented.

R1.justification: v2 makes Dufour et al.'s generative geolocalization work central to its positioning, contrasting latent multiscale diffusion with raw-coordinate diffusion and flow matching. Related work and the introduction are revised accordingly, with additional references including flow matching, SatCLIP, and GAIR. This substantially expands the relationship to relevant prior approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and experimental narrative undergo substantial rewriting. Preliminaries and parts of the encoding explanation are condensed, experiment subsections are reorganized, and appendix sections are inserted. The method name, author information, conference header, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive reflow and resizing. Table 1 becomes a three-dataset comparison, and v2 adds generative-comparison and operation-timing tables, a diffusion-step figure, and two algorithm displays. Existing figures and appendix results are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important evidence gap in v1: the latent-diffusion approach lacked direct comparisons with generative geolocalization alternatives and was evaluated on only one benchmark. Tables 1–2 substantially strengthen validation, including a spatially mismatched dataset that exposes the hybrid's limitations, while pseudocode improves inspectability. The gains outweigh the remaining weaknesses, although blanket superiority claims exceed the mixed results, notably the coverage comparisons in Table 2.
